description: Command line client for the Mautic REST API. Named credential profiles, basic auth and OAuth2, the full endpoint surface as noun-verb subcommands, and an embedded reference for AI agents via `mautic llm`.
rules: Run `mautic auth status --verify` before anything else; it works with nothing configured and names exactly what is missing.
Credentials resolve flag > environment variable > config file, and a complete set in the environment beats every named profile — that is what makes the same commands work in CI.
MAUTIC_BASE_URL may be given with or without a trailing /api; both my-mautic-assistant's MAUTIC_API_ENDPOINT (with /api) and the raw instance root are accepted and normalised.

Never hand-assemble a request body. Every writable property has a flag, unmodelled fields go through --set alias=value, and --data @file.json is only for nested structures such as campaign events or segment filters.
Contact field aliases are configured per instance: run `mautic fields list` before writing. Mautic ignores unknown properties silently, so a typo'd alias looks like a successful write.
Parse --format json, jsonl or csv. The default table truncates cells and shows a curated column subset, so parsing it produces plausible nonsense.
In --format json a list is {"total":N,"count":M,"items":[...]}: total is the whole collection, count is what this call returned. Compare them before answering "how many".
--order-by and --where take database column names in snake_case (date_identified, lead_id), not the camelCase property names in the response. A wrong column is ignored silently rather than rejected.
Segments are called lists inside Mautic: /segments returns {"lists":[...]} and one segment is {"list":{...}}. The --lists flag on emails takes segment IDs.
Anonymous visitors are contacts, so most records on a busy instance have no email; filter with --where email:isNotNull before drawing conclusions about contact counts.
Use `mautic stats query <table>` and `mautic data get <type>` for volume questions instead of paging entity endpoints; their timestamps are UTC while entity dates use the instance timezone.
`mautic emails send` mails every contact in the email's segments and cannot be recalled: run --dry-run first, read the target line on stderr, and pass --yes deliberately.

`mautic api <METHOD> <PATH>` reaches any endpoint this CLI does not wrap, reusing the same credentials, retries and --dry-run. PATH is relative to the API root, so pass /contacts and not /api/contacts.
